name: Tehri Dam — Bhagirathi River (Uttarakhand)
description: 260.5 m earth-and-rockfill dam on the Bhagirathi River, 1.5 km downstream of its confluence with the Bhilangana, near New Tehri, Uttarakhand. Tallest dam in India (1000 MW Stage-I, operated by THDC). No failure has occurred; this is a hypothetical scenario over the real Bhagirathi gorge terrain down towards Devprayag.

structure.spillway: Chute spillway (3 bays) on right bank + 2 right-bank and 2 left-bank shaft spillways

breach_event.discharge_source: No authoritative published dam-break peak-outflow figure adopted. A full breach of a 3,540 Mm3 reservoir would produce a peak outflow far in excess of the 15,540 m3/s PMF spillway design flood, but no single peer-reviewed value is cited here. Operator must supply a breach hydrograph before running.

simulation_defaults.breach_latlon_note: Public geographic reference for the dam location. Not a physics parameter.
